excerpt: Relativity Space is building the reusable Terran R rocket. Its Terran 1 history, Eric Schmidt's takeover as CEO, launch contracts and alternatives.
content:
Relativity Space is a rocket company based in Long Beach, California. Its site says it builds reusable rockets to make access to space more reliable and routine. It became known for 3D-printing large parts of its rockets. In 2023 it launched Terran 1, a small rocket made largely by 3D printing; TechCrunch reported that the flight showed the approach could work but did not reach orbit, and about a month later the company dropped Terran 1 to focus on a much larger rocket, Terran R.

Terran R is a medium-to-heavy-lift, reusable launch vehicle meant to compete with SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy. Relativity says its first launch is planned for late 2026 from Cape Canaveral, Florida. The company has reported nearly $3 billion in launch contracts, and in November 2025 the satellite operator SES signed a multi-launch agreement for Terran R flights, according to Via Satellite.

In March 2025 former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt became Relativity's CEO, succeeding cofounder Tim Ellis, who stayed on the board. TechCrunch, citing The New York Times, reported that Schmidt had made a significant investment and taken a controlling stake. Ellis had led the company since founding it; the change put one of the technology industry's best-known executives in charge of getting Terran R to the launch pad.

Relativity sells launch services to satellite operators and does not publish prices. It is on 100xFounder because it is one of the best-known space startups, and because its first Terran R launch is a milestone to watch.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
